title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Chip swell builds as the Fed wave looms
conditions.summary: Nasdaq futures edge higher on a memory-chip rally while the Dow lags. Traders are waiting for the Fed at 1 PM CT and Microsoft and Alphabet earnings after the close.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: Around 4:50 AM ET, Nasdaq-100 futures were up 0.4%, S&P 500 futures up 0.1% and Dow futures down 0.2%; Russell 2000 futures were not available in sources checked.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.02%, and the dollar index firmed toward 102.5.
WTI crude is about $101.40, up 1.5%; gold is about $4,055, down 0.5%.
Bitcoin is near $80,900, up about 1% over 24 hours; the VIX closed Tuesday near 17.5.
Asia: Korea's Kospi surged about 6.6% on SK Hynix, and the Nikkei rose about 1%.
Europe: major indexes opened about 0.1% to 0.3% lower ahead of the Fed and Big Tech earnings; Spain's IBEX fell about 1%.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: FOMC decision at 1:00 PM CT; markets widely expect a hold at 3.75%–4.00% after September's hike.
Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference is expected around 1:30 PM CT; there is no new dot plot at this meeting.
Futures traders price a strong chance of a December hike as energy-driven inflation stays elevated.
Bank of Canada rate decision at 8:45 AM CT; UK budget also out today, and the ECB decides Thursday.
September PCE inflation is due Thursday, and Q3 GDP (expected around 3.2%) is due this week.

sections.title: Earnings
items: GE Vernova: organic orders up 96% to $29.3B and revenue of $12.6B beat estimates; raised guidance, doubled its buyback and agreed to buy Trench Group for $9B.
Boston Scientific: Q3 sales up 1.5% to $5.14B, adjusted EPS $0.73; it expects Q4 sales to fall 1%–3%.
Seagate: beat on EPS and revenue and guided above consensus, but shares fell about 4% premarket after a big run.
Robinhood: revenue of $1.42B and adjusted EPS of $0.60 missed as crypto revenue fell 55%; shares down about 8%.
Visa: shares off about 1.7% after fiscal Q4 results and a softer EPS growth outlook.
After today's close: Microsoft and Alphabet, with cloud growth and AI capex in focus. Biogen also reports today.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: SKHY (SK Hynix): +7.8% — quarterly profit jumped more than sevenfold.
MU (Micron): +4% — memory-chip read-through from SK Hynix.
WDC (Western Digital): +4.5% — storage stocks lifted by the memory rally.
GOOGL (Alphabet): +1.2% — report that OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips; earnings after the close.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): +1.5% — chip sector strength.
HOOD (Robinhood): -8% — Q3 profit missed on weaker crypto trading.
STX (Seagate): -3.7% — sell-the-news despite a beat and raise.
V (Visa): -1.7% — fiscal Q4 results and a softer growth outlook.

sections.title: Business News
items: EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal valued near $12.8B, creating the largest US natural gas producer.
A banking consortium lined up $63B in financing for hardware destined for Anthropic, which filed for a US IPO on Monday.
Intel signed a deal to acquire quantum software company Classiq, reportedly for about $2.2B.
Nvidia is investing $3B in Meta's $97.5B equity offering.
Guidewire agreed to buy London insurance-software firm hyperexponential for $1.7B in cash.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 1:00 PM CT Fed decision and 1:30 PM CT Warsh press conference — watch for December hike signals.
Microsoft and Alphabet after the close — cloud growth and AI spending plans.
WTI near $100 and the 10-year near 5% — energy and rates remain the key pressure points.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Wednesday, October twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the board this morning is my co-anchor, Gus the wonder dog, freshly toweled off from the dawn patrol. Give the lineup a howdy, Gus! It's Fed day, and the water is choppy but surfable. Early this morning, Nasdaq one hundred futures were up about four tenths of a percent, S and P 500 futures were up about a tenth, and Dow futures were down about two tenths. The ten year Treasury yield sits right around five percent. Crude oil is back above one hundred dollars a barrel, and gold slipped about half a percent. Korea's Kospi exploded more than six percent on chip stocks, and Europe opened a touch lower. The big wave today is the Federal Reserve. The decision lands at one P M Central, with Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference expected at one thirty. Markets expect a hold at three point seven five to four percent after last month's hike, but traders see a good chance of another hike in December. High energy prices keep inflation sticky. On the tide chart, GE Vernova crushed it, with orders nearly doubling, revenue topping estimates, a raised outlook, and a nine billion dollar deal for Trench Group. That's a Kahuna wave of power demand from A I data centers. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Boston Scientific grew sales just one and a half percent and sees fourth quarter sales slipping. After today's close, Microsoft and Alphabet report, and the whole beach is watching their A I spending. In the lineup, S K Hynix's American shares jumped nearly eight percent after profit soared more than sevenfold. Micron rode that swell up four percent. Robinhood wiped out about eight percent after missing on profit, and Seagate slipped despite beating. Beach talk: E Q T agreed to buy Range Resources in an all stock deal worth about thirteen billion dollars, creating the biggest U S natural gas producer. And a banking group lined up sixty three billion dollars in financing for hardware headed to Anthropic, which just filed for its I P O. Sets to watch: the Fed at one P M Central, the Warsh press conference at one thirty, and Microsoft and Alphabet after the bell. Gnarly swings are possible, so don't be a kook chasing ripples. Want my call on a wave of your own? Look up any stock, E T F or futures contract in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
